name: Block Cipher Assessment
description: Assessment of block cipher implementations including AES and legacy ciphers (3DES, Blowfish). Covers algorithm selection review, mode of operation analysis (ECB, CBC, CTR, GCM), key size evaluation, padding oracle identification, and implementation weakness detection.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to block cipher concepts or assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands block cipher fundamentals and why mode selection matters
evidence: Can explain the difference between ECB, CBC, CTR, and GCM modes
Understands why ECB mode is insecure for structured data
Can identify deprecated algorithms (DES, 3DES, Blowfish) and explain their respective weaknesses (key size, block size, performance)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies block cipher configurations in systems under supervision
evidence: Extracts cipher suite configurations from TLS, application, and protocol settings
Identifies use of deprecated algorithms or weak key sizes in code review
Documents cipher findings following lab reporting templates
Uses tools (e.g., testssl.sh, OpenSSL) to enumerate cipher configurations under guidance

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses block cipher implementations and produces compliant findings
evidence: Evaluates mode-of-operation correctness including IV/nonce handling
Identifies padding oracle vulnerabilities in CBC implementations
Assesses key derivation and key management practices for symmetric keys
Produces clear, actionable findings referencing NIST SP 800-131A (e.g., TDEA disallowed for encryption after 2023), SP 800-38A, or equivalent guidance

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex or custom block cipher deployments; develops assessment tooling
evidence: Evaluates custom or non-standard cipher modes in proprietary protocols
Develops scripts or tools to automate block cipher configuration auditing
Reviews and mentors junior staff on symmetric cryptography assessment
Identifies subtle implementation flaws such as key reuse, nonce mismanagement, or timing leaks

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines block cipher assessment methodology; publishes research on cipher weaknesses
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's symmetric cipher assessment methodology
Published research on block cipher implementation vulnerabilities
Provides expert guidance on algorithm migration (e.g., 3DES to AES transitions)
Trains teams on block cipher assessment techniques and emerging threats

assessment_methods.description: Given a system with multiple symmetric cipher configurations, identify all weak or misconfigured ciphers and produce a prioritised findings report
Analyse a CBC-mode implementation and determine whether it is vulnerable to padding oracle attacks; demonstrate exploitation on a lab target
